questions.question_text:
A mortgage of $\$165\,000$ at $9\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.0075$) is repaid with monthly payments of $\$1700$.
Evaluate the balance $A_{180}$ after $15$ years ($180$ months), to the nearest cent.

options.why: Ignored the negative sign indicating the loan was already overpaid.
Used the annual interest rate with 15 years and multiplied repayments without the annuity formula ($165\,000(1.09)^{15}-1700(15)$).
Rounded intermediate powers of $(1+r)$ to two decimal places.

questions.question_text:
A business loan of $\$80\,000$ is repaid in quarterly instalments of $\$3450$ over $8$ years.
Find the total amount paid over the life of the loan.

options.why: Multiplied repayment by 8 years instead of 32 quarters.
Added the initial principal to the total payments.
Calculated total interest instead of total amount paid.

questions.question_text:
A personal loan of $\$55\,000$ is fully repaid with $60$ monthly payments of $\$1140$.
How much total interest was charged?

options.why: Reported the total amount paid rather than the interest charged.
Multiplied monthly repayment by 10 instead of computing total payments minus principal.
Calculated the average annual interest by dividing total interest by 5 years ($13\,400 \div 5$).

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$25\,000$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) has monthly repayments of $\$400$.
Find the balance owing after $24$ months, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Subtracted 24 repayments directly from principal without compounding interest.
Computed compound growth of principal but neglected repayments.
Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.

questions.question_text: For a $\$35\,000$ loan where $A_{36}=\$18\,483.69$ after $36$ monthly repayments of $\$650$, calculate the total interest charged during the first $36$ months.

options.why: Reported principal reduction instead of interest charged.
Reported total amount paid rather than interest.
Subtracted the remaining balance directly from total payments instead of computing total payments minus principal reduction.

questions.question_text: In the loan balance formula $A_{n}=PV(1+r)^{n}-M\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$, what does the subtracted term $M\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$ represent?

options.text: The future value of all $n$ repayments compounded to the end of period $n$.
The total interest accumulated on the original principal.
options.why: Confused the repayment annuity sum with total interest.

options.text: The total amount of principal remaining unpaid after $n$ periods.
options.why: Confused the repayment sum with the net balance $A_n$.

options.text: The simple sum of all $n$ repayments $n\times M$.
options.why: Ignored the compounding of individual repayments over time.

questions.solution_text:
Each repayment $M$ compounds from the moment it is paid until period $n$.
The sum $M+M(1+r)+\dots+M(1+r)^{n-1}=M\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$ represents the total future value of all $n$ repayments.

questions.question_text:
A couple takes out a $\$250\,000$ mortgage at $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.006$) with monthly payments of $\$2000$.
What is the balance owing at the end of $10$ years ($120$ months)?

options.why: Assumed exactly half the principal is repaid after half the term.
Subtracted total payments $120 \times 2000 = 240\,000$ directly from principal.
Computed compound growth of principal but neglected repayments.

questions.question_text: After $10$ years on a $20$-year mortgage with equal monthly repayments, why is the outstanding balance substantially more than $50\%$ of the initial principal?

options.text: Early repayments are predominantly consumed by interest on the large initial principal, so the principal reduces slowly at first.
The bank increases the interest rate during the first half of the loan term.
options.why: Incorrectly assumes a variable interest rate rather than constant rate mathematics.

options.text: The monthly repayments are smaller during the first 10 years.
options.why: Assumed repayments are non-equal when they are fixed equal instalments.

options.text: Compound interest only begins to accrue in the second half of the loan term.
options.why: Misunderstands the continuous compounding mechanism of reducing balance loans.

questions.solution_text:
In the early years, the debt is large, so a large fraction of each repayment pays interest.
Only a small fraction reduces the principal, meaning the balance drops slowly.
As the balance decreases, less interest is charged, accelerating principal reduction in later years.
